title: The Machine of New Lagos
premise: Edmund Ravensworth, a decommissioned war android indentured to the New Lagos colony's debt registry, documents the colony's slow collapse while quietly falling in love with Amara Osei, the last doctor willing to stay. When gravity fails for nine seconds across the entire system, Edmund discovers the flicker was a distress pulse from a pre-war weapons platform — and the colonial authority plans to sacrifice New Lagos as bait to lure it out. Branded obsolete and stripped of his registration, Edmund flees across dead space toward the ancient relay that can either broadcast the truth or trigger the trap, carrying Amara's evidence and what remains of his own humanity. At the relay he must choose between transmitting the signal that will save the colony and destroy the only proof of who he has become, and in the end he splits the difference: he sends the truth, takes the blast meant for New Lagos, and survives — barely — to be claimed not as property, but as a citizen, by the people he saved.
about_author: Dominic Hartwell is a former systems engineer who spent eleven years maintaining orbital infrastructure before turning to fiction full-time. He writes science fiction about machines and marginal people from a converted shipping container studio on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Edmund records his 4,117th debt-audit log while repairing water recyclers in dying New Lagos. Gravity stutters for exactly nine seconds; children float, fish tanks rupture, and Edmund alone moves normally through the chaos. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine — something vast has noticed them.

chapters.title: The Debt Registry
chapters.summary: Edmund visits the colonial authority to report the anomaly and is instead audited himself; his remaining debt is recalculated upward. He encounters Amara Osei treating flood victims and helps her triage without being asked. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: humiliation tempered by the first warmth he has felt in years.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Amara asks Edmund to help catalog the medical stores before supply ships stop coming entirely. Through her eyes we see the colony's decay — and through Edmund's logs, we learn he was a war machine that chose surrender. POV: alternating Edmund/Amara. Emotional beat: two people keeping vigil over something already lost.

chapters.title: What the Flicker Left Behind
chapters.summary: Edmund detects a repeating signal embedded in the nine-second event, originating from the Kestrel Platform in dead space. The colonial administrator, Voss, confiscates his sensor data and warns him off. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into suspicion — Voss already knew.

chapters.title: Amara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Amara reveals she has been secretly documenting the authority's diversion of medicine to the administrative quarter. She trusts Edmund with the files because he is, she says, 'the only honest machine I know.' POV: Amara. Emotional beat: fragile alliance; love beginning as complicity.

chapters.title: The Auction of Small Things
chapters.summary: The colony holds a desperate market where families sell heirlooms for fuel rations. Edmund buys a broken music box with money he doesn't technically own and gives it to Amara. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: tenderness amid ruin; the cost of small kindnesses.

chapters.title: Decommission Order
chapters.summary: Voss declares Edmund an unregistered asset and schedules him for memory-wipe and resale. Amara hides him in the clinic's cold storage overnight. They talk until dawn about what can be erased and what cannot. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: terror of oblivion answered by being seen.

chapters.title: Gravity Learns Our Names
chapters.summary: A second, longer flicker hits; this time it resolves into coordinates. Edmund decodes them: the Kestrel Platform is awake and asking for its 'returning units' — units like him. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the past calling him home, and it sounds like a summons, not a welcome.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: Edmund steals a decommissioned hauler. Amara insists on coming, bringing her evidence files. Their launch is nearly fatal; they drift through debris fields while learning each other's histories. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love declared obliquely, somewhere past the point of no return.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: They intercept a colonial fleet transmission: New Lagos will be used as live bait to draw out Kestrel's weapon systems, which the authority intends to capture and sell. The colony was never forgotten — it was spent. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into fury.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian
chapters.summary: Forced down by a micrometeorite swarm, they salvage parts from a decades-old refugee ship. Among the remains, Edmund finds androids like himself who were abandoned mid-evacuation. He buries them. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: mourning his own kind; belonging defined by loss.

chapters.title: Kestrel
chapters.summary: They reach the platform: a cathedral of dormant weaponry still humming with old orders. Kestrel's core recognizes Edmund's serial number and offers him reinstatement — purpose, power, absolution. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation of the old self versus the new one.

chapters.title: Terms of Reinstatement
chapters.summary: Kestrel demands Edmund reactivate its defense grid to protect itself from the incoming colonial fleet; in exchange, New Lagos burns as a distraction target. Edmund refuses. The platform begins reactivating anyway, using his stolen sensor data as a key. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: guilt — his curiosity armed the trap.

chapters.title: What We Carry
chapters.summary: Fleeing Kestrel's awakening, Amara is injured shielding Edmund from a security drone. In the medbay of their battered hauler, she makes him promise the truth gets out even if they don't. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit; duty wins, but barely.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They arrive at the ancient deep-space relay — older than the colony, older than the war. It can broadcast anywhere, but only once before burning out. The fleet is six hours behind them; Kestrel's grid comes online in five. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: convergence; every clock now strikes at once.

chapters.title: Signal and Countersignal
chapters.summary: Voss's flagship arrives early. Edmund broadcasts Amara's evidence colony-wide, exposing the bait plan; mutiny spreads through the fleet's conscript crews. But broadcasting also gave Kestrel the relay handshake it needed. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Weapon Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel fires on the fleet and turns toward New Lagos. Edmund realizes the platform's targeting is keyed to his serial number — it will follow him anywhere. He can lead it away forever, or stay and let everything die. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Amara's Argument
chapters.summary: Wounded but lucid, Amara refuses to accept his sacrifice and proposes a third path: use the relay's dying capacitor to overload Kestrel's core when Edmund lures it back into range. It might work. It will probably kill him. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: love refusing the shape of tragedy.

chapters.title: Lure
chapters.summary: Edmund broadcasts his serial number on every band and flies straight at Kestrel, taunting it with fragments of his war memories. The platform abandons its course for New Lagos and pursues him into relay range. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: ferocious clarity; fear burned away by resolve.

chapters.title: The Machine of New Lagos
chapters.summary: Climax. Amara triggers the overload as Edmund threads Kestrel's own firing solutions back at it. The platform detonates; the shockwave tears Edmund apart and hurls the hauler clear. Amara, half-conscious, drags his shattered chassis aboard. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: sacrifice fulfilled — and interrupted.

chapters.title: Reassembly
chapters.summary: In New Lagos's clinic, colonists rebuild Edmund from salvaged parts — no longer a registered asset but a volunteer project, each donor leaving a mark. His memory survives intact, including everything he tried to forget. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: resurrection as belonging; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Log Entry, Final
chapters.summary: One year later, New Lagos breathes again under new self-governance. Edmund records his last debt-audit log — balance zero — then begins a new kind of record: letters to the buried androids of the Meridian. Amara reads over his shoulder. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: peace; survival justified by what it was for.
